events.title: Kent State Shootings
events.description: Ohio National Guard soldiers opened fire on unarmed student protesters at Kent State University demonstrating against the U.S. invasion of Cambodia, killing four students and wounding nine others.
events.significance: The tragedy intensified opposition to the Vietnam War, triggered a nationwide student strike that closed hundreds of colleges, and became a lasting symbol of the divide in American society during the Vietnam era.

events.title: Margaret Thatcher Becomes UK Prime Minister
events.description: Following the Conservative Party's victory in the general election, Margaret Thatcher became the first woman to serve as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
events.significance: Thatcher governed for over eleven years, reshaping British politics and the economy through privatization, deregulation, and curbs on union power, a legacy known as Thatcherism.

events.title: Haymarket Affair
events.description: A bomb was thrown at police dispersing a labor rally in Haymarket Square, Chicago, held in support of workers striking for an eight-hour workday. The explosion and subsequent gunfire killed several police officers and civilians.
events.significance: The event led to controversial trials and executions of anarchist leaders, and it became a pivotal moment in the international labor movement, helping inspire the commemoration of International Workers' Day on May 1.

events.title: Columbus Lands in Jamaica
events.description: During his second voyage to the Americas, Christopher Columbus first sighted and landed on the island of Jamaica.
events.significance: The landing began Spanish involvement in Jamaica, which was colonized in the early 1500s, with devastating consequences for the indigenous Taíno population.

events.title: Hemingway Wins the Pulitzer Prize
events.description: Ernest Hemingway was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction for his novella The Old Man and the Sea.
events.significance: The award helped cement Hemingway's reputation and contributed to his receiving the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.
